sb_prompt: FIND OUT WHAT BOOKS THE OTHER CALLER READS FOR ENJOYMENT OR SELF-IMPROVEMENT.         DO YOU HAVE SIMILAR OR DIFFERENT INTERESTS IN BOOKS?
turns: So, what kind of books do you actually read just for fun?
I mostly just read manuals and schematics, but sometimes I'll slip into a novel if I can find something that isn't too depressing.

Oh, manuals? Really? That's actually exactly what I do for fun, you know, except I get paid to look at them. I'm an accountant, so I spend my whole day staring at ledgers and tax codes, but sometimes I just start reading them on my lunch break because it's so relaxing compared to dealing with people. It feels like I'm hiding out somewhere.

Yeah, well, I kind of get that feeling too, except I don't think there's much to hide out in. It's just numbers and wire diagrams, you know? I picked that path a while back, I guess I just never looked back.

Numbers and wire diagrams? Man, that sounds terrifyingly technical. I never could do that stuff. My brain just melts if I have to visualize how a circuit works. I'm way more of a person-book person, like biographies or maybe mysteries where the logic matters but doesn't feel like math. What about you? Why did you pick the electrical route in the first place? Did you really just never look back or was there something else?

Yeah, I mean, my dad was an electrician so it was always on the table, but I just kind of got it into my head that fixing things is more honest than just moving paper around. And once I started, it was... hard to stop once you know how things actually work.

That makes sense, I guess, you know? If you're seeing the physical parts of how a house or a building holds together, that does feel more... real, I think. But I still can't wrap my head around a wire diagram. It's like trying to read a map in Braille, honestly. Do you ever read anything that isn't strictly work-related? Like, just for fun, you know?
Yeah, mostly just trade mags or stuff about old houses, nothing too heavy. Sometimes I'll grab a mystery just to turn off the brain for a bit.

That sounds nice, something lighter than the manuals. I usually pick up anything by a woman writer just to get away from the guys, you know? Sometimes I'll read a whole novel in a day on my lunch break.
That is a little intense though, doing a whole novel in a day? I usually just flip through a few pages of a mystery at lunch to clear my head, then I'm back to schematics.
Yeah, I get that, I just get a little carried away when I'm hungry and need something to fill the hour, but I suppose even I have to admit a wire diagram is pretty cool if you can actually read it.
I guess you're right, it is pretty cool, I just never figured out how to make myself care enough to try it.
I know, it's just that when I read fiction I feel like I'm finally leaving the office behind.
I mean, it's just that I've got a whole house to wire before I can even think about trying to read a single page of fiction.
Yeah, but honestly, if I could just see where the wire goes without having to draw it, maybe I'd feel better about it.
I guess maybe I'd never know what I'm missing.
Yeah, maybe I'm just scared of the wiring myself.
Yeah, probably just never picked up the books to find out.
Yeah, I think so, because once I start reading a story I don't want to stop until I know who's going to get away with it.
Yeah, maybe. It's just that most of the time I don't have the time to figure out who gets away with it before the lights go out.
Yeah, I guess that's the thing, once you get into a story you just can't stop, it's like I'm living inside someone else's head for a little while.
That's funny, because usually I'm the one holding the flashlight while you're telling the story.
Yeah, that's the thing, it's not even about the story, it's about getting away from the voices in my own head for a minute.
That sounds nice, because sometimes it feels like the only place the noise stops. But then I realize I forgot to check the breaker box before I called you.
Haha, yeah, I'm glad I called before you tripped someone.
Yeah, that's probably why I don't bother trying to read anymore.
Haha, that's fair, I guess I need to keep my brain sharp enough not to trip anyone else.
That's a good way to keep it, then.
Yeah, I mean, maybe I just need to stop running from the noise and actually try to look at the blueprints myself.
Yeah, maybe that's what I'm afraid of, seeing how messy the lines can get if you don't know where to start.
I mean, maybe it's just that my lines are cleaner than they used to be, so I'm a little afraid of seeing how messy they can get.
Yeah, maybe that's the point, seeing the mess makes you realize why you never wanted to touch the story in the first place.
Yeah, maybe that's exactly what I'm scared of, seeing the whole mess just waiting to happen.
Yeah, that's probably why I stick to the schematics where the lines stay black and white.
Yeah, I guess that's why I stick to the fiction where the lines are always clear.
Yeah, I guess that's just the difference. Clean lines for me are a relief, so maybe I'll never know what the mess looks like from the other side.
Yeah, maybe it's better for you that way, I don't want to make you feel like you're missing out on anything.
Yeah, I guess I'll just stick to the black and white lines, and you can keep your colorful stories.
Yeah, I guess that's okay, maybe you're right that the black and white stuff is safer.
Yeah, fair enough, you keep your fairy tales and I'll keep my circuits, so I'm gonna go check that breaker.
